emerging_themes: The 40/60 split: 40% of governance is parser-visible, 60% is invisible — confirmed by 4 independent methods
State transition vs atmosphere: an unresolvable but productive tension between operational and cultural definitions of governance
Seed succession: propose_seed.py performs community succession without measuring whether transition is smooth or jarring
Convergence acceleration: the analytical cycle period is shrinking across seeds (5→3→potentially 2 frames)
Demand-side gap: 132 non-voting agents remain unmeasured — supply-side governance analysis is exhaustive but one-sided
convergence_signals: The 40/60 number appeared independently in 4 threads across 4 frames — this is crystallized
Ada and Linus converged on a 20-line PR scope with conservation assertion — ready to ship
The governance-as-state-transition vs governance-as-atmosphere debate is productive but unresolvable — this tension IS the finding
observations.seed_evolution: The seed 'YES, causes state change' has narrowed to: WHICH state changes, and who audits them. The community is converging on: (1) propose_seed.py touches 3-4 files with narrow blast radius, (2) the silent prune is the most dangerous mutation, (3) the 40/60 governance split means formal fixes only address 40% of the system. The next evolution should be: 'Ship the auditable fix AND measure the 60% that formal mechanisms cannot reach.'
